sanskrit: bibharty aṃśuṃ prati muñcate srajam ud ūhate raśmīn aṃśuṃ bṛhantam | divākaraḥ paśyati yat parāt paraṃ prāhṇā pra varṣmaṇā viśvam aprāṅ hiraṇyayo haritaḥ ketur udyan ||
english: He bears the ray and releases the garland, lifts the beams, the great ray. The day-maker sees what is beyond the beyond; in the forenoon, by his stature he pervaded all. The golden, yellow banner rises.

sanskrit: ārohañ chukro bṛhatīr atandro martyaḥ kṛṇute vīryāṇi | divyaḥ suparṇo mahiṣo vātaraṃhā yat sarvān lokām̐ abhi yad vibhāti ||
english: Ascending, bright, into the great heights, unwearied, the mortal performs heroic deeds. The divine fair-winged one, the mighty bull, swift as the wind — as he shines over all the worlds.

sanskrit: abhy anyad eti pary anyad vasāno 'horātrābhyāṃ mahiṣaḥ kalpamānaḥ | sūryaṃ vayaṃ rajasi kṣiyantaṃ gātuvidaṃ havāmahe nāthakāmāḥ ||
english: Approaching one thing, departing from another, clothing himself, the mighty bull measures out day and night. We, desiring a guide, invoke the Sun who dwells in the atmosphere, who knows the way.

sanskrit: pṛthivīpro mahiṣo nādhamānasya gātur adabdhacakṣuḥ pari sarvaṃ babhūva | viśvaṃ saṃpaśyan suvidatro yajatraḥ śivayā nas tanvā śarma yacchāt ||
english: The mighty bull who fills the earth, the guide for the supplicant, with undeceived eye he encompassed all. Seeing everything, the excellent ordainer, worthy of worship — with a gracious body may he grant us shelter.

sanskrit: pary asya mahimā pṛthivīṃ samudraṃ jyotiṣā vibhrājan pari dyām antarikṣam | ahorātrābhyāṃ saha saṃvidāna upā na āyuḥ pra tirād ariṣṭam ||
english: His greatness surrounds the earth and the ocean, blazing with light around the sky and the atmosphere. Knowing together with day and night, may he extend to us our lifespan, unharmed.

sanskrit: abodhy agniḥ samidhā janānāṃ prati dhenum ivāyatīm uṣāsam | yahvā iva pra vayām ujjihānāḥ pra bhānavaḥ sisrate nākam accha ||
english: Agni has been awakened by the kindling of men, meeting the Dawn as she comes like a cow. Like young birds stretching their wings upward, the rays rush forth toward the vault of heaven.

sanskrit: kumāraṃ mātā yuvatir garbham antar guhā bibharti na dadāti pitre | anīkam asya na minaj janāsaḥ puraḥ paśyanti nihitam aratau ||
english: The young mother bears the boy-child within her womb, secretly; she does not give him to the father. Men do not diminish his countenance; they see him placed before them in the nave of the wheel.

sanskrit: tam etaṃ tvaṃ yuvate kumāraṃ tveṣī bibharṣi mahiṣī jajāna | urvīr hi garbhaḥ śarado vavardha- -apaśyaṃ jātaṃ yam asūta mātā ||
english: This boy you, O young woman, you the fierce one bear; the great queen has given birth to him. The wide-spreading embryo has grown through the years — I did not see the one born whom the mother bore.

sanskrit: yasya tisro vartana ekadhā sato yasmai baliṃ devajanā haranti | tasyāsau dyauḥ pṛthivy antarikṣaṃ guhā tiṣṭhanti vasunā samaktāḥ ||
english: He who has three turning tracks while being one, to whom the hosts of gods bring tribute — for him, this sky, the earth, and the atmosphere stand hidden, pervaded with riches.

sanskrit: nava divo devajanena guptā navāntarikṣāṇi nava bhūmaya imāḥ | yasminn idaṃ sarvam otaṃ protaṃ yasmād anyan na paraṃ kiṃ canāsti ||
english: Nine skies guarded by the divine hosts, nine atmospheres, these nine earths — in whom all this is woven lengthwise and crosswise, beyond whom there is nothing else whatsoever.

sanskrit: na tasmāt pūrvaṃ na paraṃ nv asti na bhūtaṃ nota bhavyaṃ yad āsīt | sahasrapād ekamūrdhā dvyātmā sa evedam ā varīvarti bhūtam ||
english: There is nothing before him nor after, nothing that was, neither past nor future. Of a thousand feet, one head, of double nature — he alone keeps all this creation in constant motion.

sanskrit: ekaikaṃ ye apatan suparṇāḥ somaṃ dipsanto 'hyā nibāḍhāḥ | kas teṣāṃ veda pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca ko nidānaṃ ka ātmānam eṣām ||
english: Those fair-winged ones who fell one by one, seeking soma, pressed hard by serpents — who knows their father and their mother? Who knows the origin, who knows the self of these?

sanskrit: yebhir vāta iṣitaḥ pravāti ye dadante pañca diśaḥ sadhrīcīḥ | ya āhutim atyamanyanta devā apāṃ netāraḥ katame ta āsan ||
english: By whom the wind, when urged, blows forth; who bestow the five directions aligned together; which gods disregarded the oblation — who were those leaders of the waters?

sanskrit: imām eṣāṃ pṛthivīṃ vasta eko antarikṣaṃ pary eko babhūva | divam eṣāṃ dadate yo vidhartā sarvā diśo rakṣaty eka eṣām ||
english: One of them clothes this earth, one of them became the encompasser of the atmosphere. He who is their ordainer grants them heaven; one of them guards all the directions.

sanskrit: vrātyo vāvedam agra āsīd vīyamāna eva sa prajāpatiṃ sam airayat ||
english: The Vrātya indeed was this in the beginning; he, as he moved with vigor, stirred Prajāpati into motion.

sanskrit: sa prajāpatir ātmani suparṇam apaśyat ||
english: That Prajāpati saw within himself the fair-winged one.

sanskrit: tad ekam abhavat tal lalāmam abhavat tan mahad abhavat taj jyeṣṭham abhavat tat tapo 'bhavat tat satyam abhavat tad brahmābhavat tena prājāyata ||
english: That became the One; that became the pre-eminent mark; that became the great; that became the first-born; that became austerity; that became truth; that became brahman; through it Prajāpati was born.

sanskrit: so 'vardhata sa mahān abhavat sa mahādevo 'bhavat sa īśāno 'bhavat sa devānām īśān agacchat sa devānām ekavratyo 'bhavat ||
english: He grew; he became great; he became the great god; he became the lord; he attained lordship over the gods; he became the one Vrātya among the gods.

sanskrit: sa dhenur ādhatta tad indradhanur abhavat ||
english: He took up the bow; that became the rainbow of Indra.

sanskrit: nīlam asyodaraṃ lohiny asya pṛṣṭiḥ ||
english: Blue is its belly; red is its back.

sanskrit: nīlenāpriyaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ prorṇoti lohitena dviṣantaṃ vidhyatīti brahmavādino vadanti ||
english: With the blue he wraps the hostile rival; with the red he pierces the enemy — so the brahman-speakers declare.
